descriptive_title: Kindergarten Mathematics: Patterns and Relationships — Identify, Describe, Extend, and Create Repeating Patterns (A7.1–A7.4)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Kindergarten unit on Patterns and Relationships (A7.1–A7.4), framed as a parade led by Coco the Conductor and four Canadian animals. Includes 5 lesson plans, 5 worksheets, 7 manipulatives, a full assessment suite, and a Junior Pattern Conductor certificate.
long_description:
Bring patterns to life in your Kindergarten classroom. The Pattern Parade is a 5-day, ready-to-teach unit that takes children on a journey with Coco the Conductor and the Parade Animals — Bea the Bear, Finn the Fox, Bibi the Beaver, and Moss the Moose — to discover the magic of repeating patterns.

Each lesson is fully scripted with teacher prompts, structured for play-based learning, and includes a printable student worksheet that consolidates the day's thinking. Children build patterns with manipulatives, find the core, translate one pattern into multiple representations (animal, sound, body), fix missing pieces, and finally lead their own parade as Pattern Conductors.

What makes this unit different:
- Aligned to all four Ontario Kindergarten Patterns expectations (A7.1, A7.2, A7.3, A7.4) — no gaps, no drift.
- A single coherent narrative across 5 days: recurring characters, threaded vocabulary, an anchor chart that grows day by day.
- Four-track differentiation built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners.
- Detailed teacher script for the conceptually trickiest moment — Lesson 3 — including expected misconceptions and recovery moves.
- Manipulatives ready to print (default black and white so any classroom printer works), plus reusable assessment trackers per lesson.
- Student-friendly Junior Pattern Conductor certificate for the closing ceremony.

Designed for Canadian classrooms: Canadian animals, the spelling 'colour' throughout, references to familiar Canadian community parades, and Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions for assessment.

Total classroom time: about 200 minutes across 5 lessons. Teacher prep time: about 90 minutes one-time, then the printables are reusable next year. Suitable for Junior or Senior Kindergarten teachers in Ontario, or any teacher introducing repeating patterns and the concept of a 'core' to 4–6 year olds.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans (40 minutes each, ~200 minutes total of teaching time)
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson, with name/date fields and child-voice learning goals
1 mid-unit formative assessment ('The Same Core Check') administered between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 prompts for student self-assessment
7 printable teacher manipulatives: parade animal cards, parade strips, sound-and-movement cards, missing mystery cards, core loop frames, anchor chart word cards, and a Coco the Conductor puppet
4 class observation trackers: 1 diagnostic (Lesson 1) plus 3 formative (Lessons 2, 3, 4)
1 four-level summative rubric covering all four expectations (A7.1–A7.4)
1 summative administration guide tying the worksheet, lesson, and rubric together for the teacher
Junior Pattern Conductor certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony
Detailed expanded walkthrough for the keystone lesson (Lesson 3 — Same Beat, Different Parade), including expected student misconceptions and teacher recovery moves
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Junior or Senior Kindergarten teachers in Ontario, or any teacher introducing repeating patterns and the concept of a 'core' to 4–6 year olds. Especially valuable for teachers who want a coherent multi-day unit rather than disconnected pattern worksheets.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: Play-based, oral-first, movement-rich. Worksheets are end-of-lesson consolidation, never the main activity. Student-generated patterns are honoured. Assessment is observational and uses the Ontario Kindergarten Communication of Learning conventions: descriptive, growth-oriented, and aligned to a 4-level rubric across each expectation.
